quotes.quote: Kaldera's parliament on Wednesday approved a bill that hands operation of the Port Kessel container terminal to a private concession for 25 years.
Lawmakers passed the measure by 88 votes to 61 after a debate that ran past midnight.
The concession will be awarded through an open tender that the transport ministry said it would launch within three months.
The winning operator must keep the terminal's current workforce of about 1,400 employees for at least five years, according to the text of the bill.
The dockworkers' union said it would study the final text before deciding whether to challenge the law in court.
Shipping lines that use the port have said the terminal needs new cranes and deeper berths to handle larger vessels.

Kaldera's parliament on Wednesday postponed a vote on a bill that would hand operation of the Port Kessel container terminal to a private concession for 25 years, after opposition lawmakers requested more time to review amendments.
The concession would be awarded through an open tender run by the transport ministry.
Under the bill, the winning operator would have to keep the terminal's current workforce of about 1,400 employees for at least five years.
The dockworkers' union has said it opposes any concession that does not guarantee existing pension terms.
Shipping lines that use the port have long complained about crane breakdowns and shallow berths.
